answer.rationale: Finance mandate requires an 18% spend cut and the primary contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew. c2 confirms the prior low-cost vendor switch delivered sharp unit-cost reduction with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing last year. c6 confirms multi-year commitments with the incumbent unlocked volume pricing without narrowing scope. Pairing the two memories suggests the lowest-TCO path: a multi-year commitment to the low-cost vendor, leveraging the incumbent's willingness-to-move (per c4/c6 dynamics) into vendor leverage on terms. The 94% utilization with no buffer argues against deferral (c5-style) since service continuity and delivery risk dominate TCO; c1 stability benefits are outweighed by the mandated cost reduction. c3's second-sourcing value is preserved as a parallel hedge but cannot be the primary lever because adding a second source doesn't directly hit the 18% cost-cut target on the largest line. Verification of c2 and c6 before committing prevents anchoring on potentially stale records and validates that unit-cost gains and multi-year pricing leverage still hold under current market conditions.
